paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, friend: you don't have to climb out of the dust before you can talk to God. The writer starts with his soul cleaving to the dust, and the first thing he does is ask the LORD, "revive me according to Your word." He asks it again in verse 37 and again in verse 40, and nobody in the psalm acts like that's too many times. When you're low, the word of God is where the reviving comes from (Psalm 119:25, 37, 40).

Notice how much of this psalm is asking. Teach me, make it clear, give me understanding, direct me, turn my heart, turn my eyes. This man loves God's word and he still says he needs help to follow it. I find that a relief, because I have never once gotten a cookie perfect by wanting it really hard (Psalm 119:26, 27, 34, 35, 36, 37). Following God is something the LORD teaches and gives. It isn't something you muscle through alone.

And look where all that asking leads. He picks the way of truth, he walks in freedom, he runs, he delights, and he won't be ashamed to speak of God's testimonies before kings (Psalm 119:30, 32, 45, 46). He says he loves these commandments, and he lifts his hands to them (Psalm 119:47, 48). So here's the big idea, baker: stay close to the word, keep asking the LORD for help, and let Him lift you from the dust. That's how a heart gets enlarged (Psalm 119:32).
